text:
maria: Heads-up — planning schema change to add accounts.external_id (nullable) next WED in the 02:00-03:00 UTC change window. Backfill for missing rows included. Need canary + version pin for read path. PTAL.
ajay: Quick Q — are we adding an index as well or relying on the backfill to populate values only? backfill could be heavy.
oliver: Index not in this PR. For backfill we'll do chunked updates: LIMIT 10k + ORDER BY id, small sleep. Recommend backfill-mode 'throttled' via deploybot.
deploy-bot: deploybot: pre-schedule check: slot open 02:00-03:00 UTC. Tag=schem/accounts-externalid. Canary targets=3 pods. Preconditions: replica_lag < 15s, migration_sql_present=true.
lin: Needs explicit rollback SQL in the PR and a short runbook (abort criteria + escape hatch). Confirm migration is add column without default to avoid table rewrite.
samir: I'll be oncall that window. Please include a short runbook here with the exact abort steps and who to ping.
maria: SQL snippet for migration (will push full file to PR):
```
ALTER TABLE accounts ADD COLUMN external_id text NULL;
-- backfill: UPDATE accounts SET external_id = generate_external_id() WHERE external_id IS NULL ORDER BY id LIMIT 10000;
```
ajay: For locking: the ADD COLUMN is metadata-only for Postgres since nullable w/o default, but the UPDATE backfill acquires row locks. We'll need to watch for long-running tx.
oliver: Backfill plan: run with ORDER BY id LIMIT 10k, commit each chunk, pause 250ms between chunks. Monitor tx lock_wait and replica lag. If replica lag > 20s, abort.
deploy-bot: deploybot: running preflight checks... replica_lag: 5s (ok), schema_migration_sql: present (ok). Ready to start canary at 02:00 UTC.
ajay: Suggest pin read-side service to v2.3.7 for canary pods only. Fallback: automatic pin to v2.3.6 if p99 latency >200ms or error rate >1%.
lin: Added a one-paragraph release note draft to the PR: "Adds nullable external_id to accounts. Zero-downtime add column; controlled backfill. No expected user-facing change."
maria: I'll add runbook bullets here now: 1) start canary; 2) run single-chunk backfill test; 3) monitor lock_wait, replica lag, p99; 4) if thresholds hit -> abort backfill + disable write jobs + notify oncall; 5) rollback service pin if needed. @samir you good to be primary?
samir: :thumbsup: I'll lead. If long locks show up we'll abort backfill and roll forward reads to pinned older version.
maria: Add alert thresholds: lock_wait > 60s, replica_lag > 20s, p99 latency > 200ms. Also add a migration-backfill-check metric.
deploy-bot: deploybot: canary started 02:00 UTC. Observability: p99 steady at baseline. Ready to proceed to rollout? React with :eyes: to indicate approval.
oliver: :eyes: approve canary rollout.
ajay: Approve.
lin: Approved — schedule 100% rollout at 02:30 UTC, with automatic hold if any threshold crossed.
deploy-bot: deploybot: starting rollout at 02:30 UTC to 100%. Monitoring mirror: p99 ok, replica_lag spiked to 22s on db-replica-2 at 02:33 UTC. Triggering rollback policy: replica_lag > 20s.
maria: Ack — initiating manual rollback steps and notifying DB team.
samir: Rolling back now: disabling backfill, triggering service pin to v2.3.6, aborting in-flight backfill transactions.
deploy-bot: deploybot: rollback initiated by samir. Rollback policy executed: pin to v2.3.6, cut canary to 0. Rolling back application at 02:34:15 UTC.
deploy-bot: deploybot: rollback complete at 02:36:30 UTC. Notes: column was added (DDL applied), backfill aborted mid-chunk. No customer-visible errors were reported, but replica_lag exceeded safe threshold.
maria: Will file follow-up ticket for controlled backfill with leader-coord + finer throttling + replica-aware pacing. Thanks for quick responses.
lin: Post-rollback action items: 1) add pre-deploy replica-lag gating to deploybot; 2) rehearse abort sequence in the next runbook drill; 3) document the feature-flag roll forward steps.
ajay: Also add a db-side lease so only one backfill runner runs at a time across regions.
samir: I'll join the follow-up meeting to own the next window.
maria: Thanks everyone — I'll attach the migration SQL + runbook to the PR and link the follow-up ticket here when created.
